target_customer: Law firms and attorneys running M&A and venture financing due diligence
problem: Reviewing data rooms for liability caps, change of control triggers and other issues takes days of attorney time. Mage automates classification, extraction and memos.

founders.name: Raffi Isanians
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a former M&A and startup attorney and gives no education.

technical_complexity.rationale: LLM extraction over large data rooms with accuracy needs is standard AI engineering with hard parts around precision, security (the site claims SOC 2 Type II) and multi language documents.

defensibility.rationale: Workflow depth helps, but Harvey, Luminance and Kira already served diligence and general models improve fast.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Harvey later announced data room partnerships and diligence tooling per its blog; no move against Mage specifically was found.

market_need_then: Diligence is a heavy billable task for lawyers, and the founder came from the work, but no dated demand statistics were found.

identity.visual_style: Clean, product focused with mock interface screenshots
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and direct, imperative headlines such as 'You run the deal. Mage manages everything else.'

branding.community_and_virality: Sponsor listing at a 2026 LegalTechTalk event per search results; founder interviewed on a Fondo startup podcast.

brand_strength.rationale: A branding search found no naming story. The brand has conference and podcast presence but little brand press.

outcome_analysis: Mage Legal is an active Summer 2024 YC company with a lawyer founder and a live product site. No outcome news was found, and well funded legal AI rivals are consolidating the space, so the record shows no clear result yet.
notes: Caplight lists a seed of $500K dated 2024-07 and Dealroom lists $125K; both unverified and conflicting, so no round is recorded. Competitor search results were 2026 vendor content, so none are listed as of founding; Luminance (founded 2015) and Kira are noted here as existing diligence tools without a dated source near the batch. Completeness pass: the 500K seed dated 2024-07 rests on Caplight alone, a single database; Dealroom lists 125K, which conflicts and is not summed.
